newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand took a breather on Friday, helped by the Reserve Bank, after sharp losses on Monday but forex traders said the unit's woes were far from over.
They anticipated a renewed assault at the start of trade on Tuesday -- after the long week-end -- on the back of continued foreign and importer dollar demand.
Some noted that moves were exaggerated due to thin pre-holiday volumes and anticipated a re-test of the unit's all time low level of around 4.76 and even beyond that to 4.78.
The rand ended at 4.7290/7340 on the dollar from 4.7510/7560 at the end of Thursday's hectic trade when it shed more than eight and a half cents on the day.
Thursday's slide was prompted by strong dollar demand as London investment houses unwound bond positions and panic short-term covering by local importers, some of which were caught off guard.
"The Reserve Bank showed more of a presence today (Friday) and helped push the rand lower but there is still dollar demand around and the market is nervous," a senior forex trader said.
"Next week is the last gasp before year-end and it could still be fairly volatile," he added.
Forex traders anticipated the rand to move in a 4.70 to 4.78 range on the dollar.
Another trader said the central bank had showed its hand more aggressively on Friday but he expected further weakness early next week, possibly up to the 4.78 level.
Traders said the rand had shifted into a new 4.72 to 4.76 short-term trading range after Thursday's sharp falls.
The rand reached an all-time low bid of around 4.76 on the dollar on October 31 this year, according to a Reserve Bank spokesman.

Against the crosses, the rand was last trading slightly better at 7.8485/8582 against sterling from 7.8520/8650 on Thursday when it slid nearly 10 cents. On the mark it was last at 0.3260/3263 from 0.3248/3252 before.
Bonds lost on the day, depressed by the rand's fall and continued money market pressure.
At 1419 GMT the key R150 bond was at 16.18 percent from 16.14 percent late on Thursday after an intraday low of 16.24 percent.
Bond traders said the market crashed through some serious support levels on Thursday (such as the 16 percent level) amid thin volumes and the outlook for next week was negative.
"The money market is looking bad with short-end rates rising over the last few days and then, of course, there's the rand...," a bond trader said.
He said the day had been characterised by mild offshore selling amid thin volumes.
Traders said it was possible bonds could weaken to the 16.75 percent level next week.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net sellers of 198.05 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 89.99 million rand's worth bonds on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 33.09 rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 2.11 billion rand on Wednesday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were quoted higher at 17.40 percent offered from 17.20 and 17.35 percent, while the 90-day BA rate also moved higher to between 16.70 and 17.00 percent from 16.65 and 16.95 percent previously.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage higher at 9.788 billion rand on Thursday from 9.650 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
